items.text: You may have heard of the idiom 'once in a blue moon' to describe an event that doesn't happen often.
But can the Moon really be blue?
Our closest neighbour in this vast galaxy, the Moon, orbits the Earth like a natural satellite.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: Our closest neighbour in this vast galaxy

items.text: Unlike many of the other planets in our Solar System, ours only has the one moon.
If you flew to it, you would land on grey rocks.
This is because the lunar surface is made from mostly magnesium, iron and other minerals of that colour.

level1.label: 表语从句
level1.text: because the lunar surface is made from mostly magnesium, iron and other minerals of that colour

items.text: But, if you're lucky to have clear skies under the curtain of night, you may be able to admire its luminosity.

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: if you're lucky to have clear skies under the curtain of night

items.text: You might even see that it seems to change shape and hue.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that it seems to change shape and hue

items.text: It's important to understand that the Moon reflects light from the Sun as it orbits the Earth, and that light bounces back to the Earth.
The position of the Moon, Sun and the Earth determines how much of the Moon we see.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: The position of the Moon, Sun and the Earth

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: how much of the Moon we see

items.text: The new Moon appears almost invisible in the sky as it is in total darkness.

level1.label: 原因状语从句
level1.text: as it is in total darkness

items.text: This is the opposite to the full Moon which is completely lit up.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the opposite to the full Moon which is completely lit up

items.text: There are eight different phases to the lunar cycle between a full Moon and a new Moon, each lasting around 28 days.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: eight different phases to the lunar cycle between a full Moon and a new Moon

items.text: In fact, the word 'month' takes its root from 'Moon' because it was almost equal to the lunar phases.

level1.label: 原因状语从句
level1.text: because it was almost equal to the lunar phases

items.text: The other phases include the crescent, quarter and gibbous phase.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: the crescent, quarter and gibbous phase

items.text: Crescent originates from the Latin verb 'crescere', meaning 'to increase', and so it is the phase just before and after a new Moon as it takes a concave shape.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: the phase just before and after a new Moon

level1.label: 时间状语从句
level1.text: as it takes a concave shape

items.text: The quarter will show half of the Moon.
'Gibbous' gets its root from the Latin term 'gibbous' which applied to the Moon's convex shape.
These shapes are determined by the adjectives 'waning', to get smaller, and 'waxing', to get bigger.
So now you know how we've named the shapes, what about those mesmerising colours?
The light waves that reach our eyes can vary due to the Moon's position on the horizon and pollution.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: The light waves that reach our eyes

items.text: This is known as Rayleigh scattering.
When the Moon is low, light travels through the densest part of the atmosphere and shorter waves of blue scatter away.
This leaves only the red and orange light waves to reach us.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: only the red and orange light waves to reach us

items.text: A warmer atmosphere, as well as smoke from wildfire, may increase the scattering effect as well, making the Moon appear less dull in spring and summer.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: A warmer atmosphere, as well as smoke from wildfire

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: making the Moon appear less dull in spring and summer

items.text: This is why it's more likely for you to look up and see a pink Moon in April, a golden Moon in May and July, and even a red coloured Moon in the month of June.

level1.label: 表语从句
level1.text: why it's more likely for you to look up and see a pink Moon in April, a golden Moon in May and July, and even a red coloured Moon in the month of June
